lines.text: Nearly a thousand islands in the South Pacific, settled long ago and fought over in a world war. This is the story of the Solomon Islands.
The islands had been home to seafaring peoples for thousands of years when, in 1893, Britain made them a protectorate.
In 1942 the Americans built a base on Guadalcanal, and around it grew Honiara, today's capital.
For months Allied and Japanese forces fought on land, at sea and in the air for Guadalcanal, and the Allied victory halted Japan's advance.
In 1943 Peter Kenilorea was born, who would become the country's first prime minister.
In 1955 came Manasseh Sogavare, four times prime minister, who in 2019 switched the country's ties from Taiwan to China.
In 1968 Jeremiah Manele was born, who became prime minister in 2024.
In 1978 the Solomon Islands became independent from Britain.
In 1998 East Rennell, with the largest lake of the Pacific islands, was listed as a World Heritage Site.
After years of unrest, an Australian-led mission arrived in 2003 to restore order, and stayed until 2017.
From a wartime battlefield to a young nation, the Solomon Islands have found their own voice.
